data: Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.

Three Falcon 9 first-stage cores strapped together, with the two side boosters returning to land while the center core lands downrange on a drone ship. Presently among the most-powerful operational heavy-lift rockets, with payload capacity rivalling Saturn V on a cost-per-kg basis far below it. (As of mid-2026, Starship has demonstrated increasingly operational capability.)
USA-358 / USSF-52 — 434 days on orbit, Vandenberg SFB
First mission to a metal-rich M-class asteroid; first interplanetary spacecraft to use Hall-effect thrusters
First mission dedicated to characterising the habitability of an icy moon; largest spacecraft NASA has ever launched for a planetary mission (6065 kg, 100-m² solar arrays)
USSF reusable robotic spaceplane — multi-year classified orbital missions, the only US spaceplane operational after the Shuttle's retirement
Launched Apollo 8, 9 and 11–17 (Apollo 9 in Earth orbit; Apollo 10 flew from 39B); today flies Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, and Crew Dragon
First mission to a metal-rich M-class asteroid
First mission dedicated to characterising Europa's habitability
Heavy-lift backbone of the Chinese space program
Heavy lift for Artemis lunar program
Nine engines, one booster, flown and re-flown dozens of times
Booster B1023, flown as a Falcon 9 first stage and as a side booster on the first Falcon Heavy (2018)
